coord_notes.kind: Weight-space reparametrisation: \(W=W_0+\Theta_2^\top\sigma(\Theta_1^\top W_0)\) (the catalog's \(f^\top=\sigma(W_0^\top\Theta_1)\Theta_2\) transposed), run in the original architecture; the update is \(\theta_0\)-dependent, so the method is not additive in the sense of Def I.2.
coord_notes.shape: The update is linear in \(\Theta_2\), so the image is a cone with vertex \(\theta_0\) inside \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\). With GELU/SiLU and \(W_0\) of full column rank it is all of \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) (the range of \(\sigma\) contains a neighbourhood of \(0\)); when \(d_{out}+r\le d_{in}\) it is a proper sub-cone of dimension \(2mr\). With ReLU and \(W_0\) of full column rank its \(A\)-part \(\sigma(\Theta_1^\top W_0)\) ranges over entrywise nonnegative factors.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\Theta_2=0\) is a zero gate (Lemma II.4): \(S_1=\{X\sigma(\Theta_{1,0}^\top W_0)\}\) has dim \(mr<d\) (checked numerically), a \(\mathrm T_A\)-type apex whose frame is read off \(W_0\).
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) acts only through \(\sigma^{-1}\), plus translations of \(\Theta_1\) along the left kernel of \(W_0\). For full-rank \(W_0\) and smooth \(\sigma\) the generic fibre has dimension \(r\max(0,m+r-n)\), i.e. \(d=\min(2mr,\,r(m+n-r))\): \(r^2+r(m-\operatorname{rk}W_0)\) when \(d_{out}\ge d_{in}\), trivial when \(d_{out}+r\le d_{in}\) (Jacobian rank, GELU and SiLU: fibres 8, 4, 0, 2 at \((m,n,r)=(8,6,2),(6,6,2),(5,9,2),(6,7,2)\)). With ReLU the gauge is linear \(GL_r\) only on the chamber \(\Theta_1^\top W_0>0\).
coord_notes.covariance: Output side \(GL_m\), absorbed by \(\Theta_1\). Input side: scalars (also absorbed by \(\Theta_1\)) times the monomials that commute with the entrywise \(\sigma\) (Lemma VI.2): positive monomials for ReLU, permutations for GELU/SiLU. So \(GL\times\mathrm{Mon}\), the mirror of the Mon×GL key. Numerically (GELU, \((m,n,r)=(3,7,1)\)), input permutations, input homotheties and output \(GL_3\) map the image onto the image to \(10^{-15}\), while a generic input \(GL_7\) leaves a residual of 3.3.
coord_notes.merge: \(f(W_0;\theta)\) is computed once after training and added to \(W_0\): the non-linearity is on the parameter side.
coord_notes.rebasing: The shape is recomputed from the merged base (as for HiRA). It is closed under real scaling through \(\Theta_2\), so cycles converge to the span, which is all of \(\Theta\) when \(\sigma(\mathrm{row}\,W_0)\) spans \(\mathbb R^{n}\).

methods.categorical_reading: PEANuT is a \(\theta_0\)-dependent object over LoRA: \(\rho=\theta_0+\Theta_2^\top\sigma(\Theta_1^\top\theta_0)\) factors through LoRA by \(h=(\Theta_2^\top,\sigma(\Theta_1^\top W_0))\), so it is LoRA's cone with a non-linear chart whose \(A\)-frame is computed from the base point (the whole cone when \(d_{out}\ge d_{in}\), a sub-cone when \(d_{out}+r\le d_{in}\)). Conversely, with \(W_0\) of full column rank, LoRA\(_r\) embeds in PEANuT\(_{2r}\) through \(\sigma(x)-\sigma(-x)=x\), which holds for ReLU, GELU and SiLU alike.

arrows.note: Pointed at LoRA's \(\mathrm T_A\) point \((0,\sigma(\Theta_{1,0}^\top W_0))\). Smooth for GELU/SiLU; for ReLU, smooth near any \(q_0\) where \(\Theta_{1,0}^\top W_0\) has no zero entry.

obstructions.reason: Every point of Im HiRA vanishes wherever \(W_0\) does (Prop II.9(e)), while PEANuT's update \(\Theta_2^\top\sigma(\Theta_1^\top W_0)\) is dense, so Im PEANuT is not inside Im HiRA when \(W_0\) has zeros. For \(W_0\) without zeros, Im HiRA \(=W_0+W_0\odot\mathcal M_{\le r}\), and a generic rank-one update \(uv^\top\) would need \(uv^\top\oslash W_0\in\mathcal M_{\le r}\), which generically has full rank; so the inclusion fails for \(r<\min(m,n)\) as well, although both methods condition on \(W_0\).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived all seven coordinates; agree. numpy (GELU, SiLU): d = min(2mr, r(m+n-r)) and S_1 = mr at Theta_2 = 0 (apex) at four shapes; image covariance under input permutations/homotheties and output GL to 1e-15, broken (3.3) by a generic input GL. Changes: (1) gauge note now gives the general fibre r max(0, m+r-n); (2) shape note: image is all of W_0 + M_{<=r} for GELU/SiLU with full column rank, a 2mr-dim sub-cone when d_out + r <= d_in; (3) covariance note adds input homotheties (absorbed by Theta_1) and the numerical check; (4) categorical reading: 'sub-object' -> 'object over LoRA', and the LoRA_r -> PEANuT_2r embedding holds for GELU/SiLU too (sigma(x)-sigma(-x)=x, checked); (5) HiRA obstruction: replaced 'zero pattern is an absolute invariant' (only zeros of W_0 persist) and added the zero-free W_0 case. LoRA arrow (A3) verified, pointed at the T_A point (0, sigma(Theta_{1,0}^T W_0)).

coord_notes.kind: A \(T\)-point over token positions: \(a(t)=q\) for \(t\ge t_{inv}\) and \(a(t)=q_0\) before, so \(\rho\circ a\) takes only the values \(\theta_0\) and \(W_0+BA\). It is a hard positional router between the frozen model and one LoRA.
coord_notes.shape: No single weight-space image: different positions see different weights, so the method is compared through the realisation \(\Phi\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(B=0\) gives the frozen function at every position. At activated positions the first-order image is LoRA's \(\{XA_0\}\) (function-level zero gate, Lemma II.4).
coord_notes.gauge: LoRA's \(GL_r\) on the single adapter.
coord_notes.covariance: At each activated position the update is LoRA's basis-free cone.
coord_notes.merge: Thm VI.3(a): a position-gated edit has no position-independent weight to absorb it, so it is M∞. Keeping the prefix KV cache equal to the base model's is the design goal.
coord_notes.rebasing: n/a: nothing can be merged into the base, so merge-and-restart is undefined.

methods.categorical_reading: Activated LoRA is LoRA pulled back along a position gate: a family \(T\to Q\) that sits at \(q_0\) before the invocation token, so its realisation \(\Phi\circ\rho\circ a\) is not \(\Phi_f(\theta)\) for any single \(\theta\). Being pointed before \(t_{inv}\) is what makes the base KV cache reusable, and it is also what blocks merging.

obstructions.reason: At function level the realised map (\(W_0\) on the prefix, \(W_0+BA\) after \(t_{inv}\)) lies outside \(\Phi_f(\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{LoRA})\) for generic prompts, so no weight-space LoRA lifts it (M∞). At each single position the update is still a LoRA update.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: F_T over token positions (hard positional gate between theta_0 and one LoRA), Fun, apex (B = 0 frozen at every position; first-order image {XA_0} at activated positions), GL_r, GLxGL, Minf (Thm VI.3(a) names Activated LoRA explicitly), rebasing n/a. The O1 obstruction to LoRA is valid generically. No changes. Consolidation (2026-10-01): rebasing 'n/a' -> null (axis undefined; '–' of VIII.B; 'n/a' is not a value in axes.json).

coord_notes.kind: At inference the sampler is off and \(\rho=W_0+sB\mu\). The Gaussian-mixture, Wishart and Dirichlet sampler on \(A\) changes only the training signal, so this is a stochastic trained method on LoRA.
coord_notes.gauge: LoRA's \(GL_r\) on \((B,\mu)\). The variational parameters do not enter \(\rho\) at inference, so they lie entirely in the generic fibre.
coord_notes.base_point: \(B=0\) as in LoRA: the \(\mathrm T_A\) apex at \(A_0=\mu_0\).

methods.categorical_reading: MonteCLoRA is LoRA times an inert factor: LoRA \(\to\) MonteCLoRA \(\to\) LoRA (freeze the variational coordinates, then project them out), so the two simulate each other without being isomorphic. Everything it adds is trained-method data: a stochastic cotangent signal for \(A\) plus KL penalties.

arrows.note: Projection forgetting the variational parameters \(\xi\). The reverse inclusion is A2 (freeze \(\xi\) at \(\xi_0\)).

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: inference map W_0 + sB mu is LoRA's, the variational parameters lie in the fibre, so R / Cone / apex (T_A at A_0 = mu_0) / GL / GLxGL / M1 / span. The projection arrow h(B, mu, xi) = (B, mu) satisfies rho_LoRA o h = rho and is pointed; the reverse A2 freezing arrow also holds. No changes.

coord_notes.kind: The forward map is LoRA's. Only the cotangent side changes: \(\nabla_A\) is computed from rank-1 sub-token reconstructions \(\hat x\), which modifies \(\mathsf R[\rho]\) and not \(\rho\). It is not kind B, whose forward map is \(\mathrm{id}_\Theta\). With \(v\) fixed, \(\hat x=\Pi x\) for the fixed projector \(\Pi=I_{n/M}\otimes vv^\top/\lVert v\rVert^2\) of rank \(n/M\), so \(\nabla_A=sB^\top G\Pi\). Under (momentum) SGD \(A\) therefore stays in \(A_0+\mathbb R^{r\times n}\Pi\), a sub-cone of LoRA's reach; Adam's coordinatewise normalisation leaves that subspace, so the restriction is optimizer-dependent and the object stays LoRA.
coord_notes.gauge: LoRA's \(GL_r\). But \(B\) and \(A\) now receive different cotangents (\(G\) and \(\hat G=\delta\hat x^\top\)), so the update is not of the form \(\Lambda D\rho^\top\gamma\), and the charge \(\Phi\) of Thm III.5 is not conserved.
coord_notes.covariance: The image is LoRA's (GL×GL). The backward compression groups consecutive input features into sub-tokens and projects them on a fixed \(v\), which is only \(\Pi\)-covariant (a block partition of input coordinates).

methods.categorical_reading: VeLoRA keeps LoRA's object and replaces its backward lens by an approximate one: the \(A\)-block is fed \(\hat G\) while \(B\) is fed the true \(G\). By Thm III.5 this block-dependent cotangent breaks LoRA's Noether charge, which is the dynamical cost of the activation-memory saving.

arrows.note: Same object; only the trained-method data (the cotangent signal for \(A\)) differ.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived; coordinates agree (the object is LoRA; only the A-cotangent is compressed). The Phi non-conservation claim checked: dPhi/dt = s(B^T(G^-G)A^T + A(G^-G)^T B) is generically nonzero. Change: kind note now records that with fixed v the reconstruction is a fixed rank-(n/M) projector, so under SGD the A-trajectory is confined to A_0 + R^{r x n} Pi (not under Adam). Arrow h = id to LoRA verified.

coord_notes.kind: Post hoc on trained factor tuples: \((B_i,A_i)\mapsto(B_i-\bar B^{gen},A_i-\bar A^{gen})\), followed by Arrow's token routing (an \(F_X\) family) over the residual experts.
coord_notes.shape: The deployed object is Arrow's input-dependent mixture, so it lives at function level. The subtraction itself has no image germ.
coord_notes.base_point: No parameter value reproduces \(f\): the subtracted experts are routed by Arrow at every input, so the realised function differs from \(f\) for generic inputs. Parameterless post-hoc operations are classified unpointed throughout (Model Soups, AdapterSoup, LoRA Switch / LoRA Composite).
coord_notes.gauge: n/a for a P operation. The factor-wise subtraction is not \(\prod GL_r\)-invariant (Prop V.4(a)), so a residual expert is not a function of the trained adapters \(B_iA_i\).
coord_notes.covariance: The factor-wise subtraction alone commutes with \(B\mapsto gB\), \(A\mapsto Ah^{-1}\) (GL×GL-equivariant on factor tuples, while still gauge-dependent). But the deployed object routes each token by \(|v_i^\top h|\), with \(v_i\) the top right singular vector of the residual expert (Arrow). That frame is natural only under conformal output and orthogonal input changes of basis, so the composite is \(CO(m)\times O(n)\subseteq\) CO×CO: the spectral-frame key.
coord_notes.merge: Arrow routes per token and per layer (input-dependent gates): M∞.
coord_notes.rebasing: n/a: no training, so nothing is restarted.

methods.categorical_reading: GenKnowSub is a post-hoc map on factor tuples composed with Arrow's \(F_X\) router. It subtracts factors rather than products, and \((B_i-\bar B)(A_i-\bar A)=B_iA_i-B_i\bar A-\bar BA_i+\bar B\bar A\) depends on the gauge representatives. By Prop V.4 it is well defined only after a joint gauge fixing, such as a shared frozen \(A\).

obstructions.reason: The residual expert \((B_i-\bar B)(A_i-\bar A)\) differs from the task-vector difference \(B_iA_i-\tfrac1G\sum_gB^{gen}_gA^{gen}_g\) by cross terms, and it changes under \((B_i,A_i)\mapsto(B_ig^{-1},gA_i)\). So it does not factor through product-level arithmetic.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived kind (P, followed by Arrow's F_X routing), shape Fun, base point and gauge n/a (no trainable Q), merge Minf, rebasing n/a. Change: covariance GLxGL -> OxO. GLxGL holds only for the subtraction on factor tuples; the deployed pipeline routes by the top right singular vector of each residual expert, which is CO(m) x O(n)-natural only, and shape/merge were already read on the deployed object. O1 obstruction to task arithmetic verified: the cross terms B_i Abar, Bbar A_i lie outside span{B_jA_j}. Consolidation (2026-10-01): base_point 'n/a' -> 'unpointed' (axis definition; as for the other parameterless P operations); gauge 'n/a' -> null (axis undefined; '–' of VIII.B; 'n/a' is not a value in axes.json); rebasing 'n/a' -> null (axis undefined; '–' of VIII.B; 'n/a' is not a value in axes.json).

coord_notes.kind: Extends \(f\) to a deeper network \(\tilde f=\ell_{\pi(L')}\circ\cdots\circ\ell_{\pi(1)}\) with tied base weights and one LoRA per replica. At \(B=0\) this is the stacked network, not \(f\), and low-rank LoRAs cannot turn a replicated block into the identity, so there is no neutral point.
coord_notes.shape: The extended network is compared with \(f\) only through realisations.
coord_notes.base_point: Unpointed relative to \((\Theta,\theta_0)\): \(\tilde f(\theta_0,q_0,-)\ne f(\theta_0,-)\). It is pointed only relative to the replicated model.
coord_notes.gauge: \(\prod_jGL_r\): one LoRA gauge per replica.
coord_notes.covariance: Each replica's update is a basis-free LoRA cone, and replication is basis-free.
coord_notes.merge: Each replica's LoRA fuses into a materialised copy of its block. The replicas share \(W_{0,\pi(j)}\), and Thm VI.3 requires an unshared target box, so the fuse is possible only after untying (one dense copy per replica). It never returns to the depth-\(L\) architecture.
coord_notes.rebasing: Per replica, merge-and-restart reaches the full block weight (LoRA's span), at the cost of untying the replicas.

methods.categorical_reading: Layer replication is an unpointed extension: the depth-upscaled network lives over a larger \(\Theta\times\Theta'\) with tied weights, and no parameter value recovers \(f(\theta_0,-)\), so it is not an object of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\). The per-replica LoRAs are ordinary pointed objects over the replicated base point.

obstructions.reason: The realised functions of the depth-\(L'\) network are generically not \(\Phi_f(\theta)\) for any \(\theta\) of the depth-\(L\) architecture, so no lift into LoRA, or into any object of \(\mathsf{Meth}(\Theta,\theta_0)\), exists.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: E0 (no parameter value recovers f, since a low-rank update cannot zero a full-rank W_o or W_down), Fun, unpointed, prod GL_r, GLxGL, M1, span per replica. The O1 obstruction to LoRA is valid generically. Change: merge note now states that M1 holds only after untying the shared replicas (Thm VI.3's unshared-box side condition).

coord_notes.kind: Selective fine-tuning: the trainable set is a fixed collection \(\mathcal S\) of whole tensors with the lowest condition numbers. KappaTune-LoRA attaches LoRA to \(\mathcal S\) instead and then has LoRA's coordinates.
coord_notes.shape: \(\theta_0+\bigoplus_{W\in\mathcal S}\mathbb R^{m_W\times n_W}\), a coordinate-block subspace.
coord_notes.covariance: Inside a selected tensor the image is all of \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) (GL×GL). The selection statistic \(\kappa=\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}\) is invariant only under \(CO(m)\times CO(n)\), so a general change of basis can move a tensor into or out of \(\mathcal S\).
coord_notes.rebasing: With the mask fixed, cycles gain nothing. Recomputing \(\kappa\) after merging could change \(\mathcal S\).

methods.categorical_reading: KappaTune is the coordinate sub-object of full fine-tuning spanned by a spectrally chosen block of tensors, i.e. full FT with the complement frozen. Its only dependence on \(\theta_0\) is through the CO×CO-invariant \(\kappa\): a spectral selection at the granularity of whole tensors.

obstructions.reason: A selected tensor moves in all \(mn\) directions, with rank up to \(\min(m,n)\). Both \(d\) and the maximal rank exceed LoRA\(_r\)'s, so LoRA\(_r\) on the same tensor cannot simulate it.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived (paper's whole-tensor variant): R / Lin / regular / none / OxO (kappa = sigma_max/sigma_min is CO x CO-invariant; non-conformal changes of basis can change the selection) / M1 / idempotent with the mask fixed. The O2 obstruction to LoRA_r holds by the max-rank criterion. KappaTune-LoRA (the HF helper's output) has LoRA's coordinates, as noted. No changes.

coord_notes.shape: \(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), of dimension \(r(m+n-r)\) and maximal rank \(r\).
coord_notes.base_point: \(\mathrm T_A\) stratum (\(B_0=0\), \(\operatorname{rank}A_0=r\)): \(S_1=\{XA_0\}\), deficit \(r(n-r)\) (Thm II.2). HF's embedding default is \(\mathrm T_B\); `init_lora_weights=\"orthogonal\"` lies outside the three strata.
coord_notes.gauge: \(GL_r\) acting by \((Bg^{-1},gA)\): the \(\mathfrak{so}_r\) half gives isometries, the \(\mathrm{Sym}_r\) half the charges \(\Phi\).

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA is the determinantal cone \(\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) pointed at its apex: the reference object of the slice, with gauge \(GL_r\) on the internal wire and merging as the canonical map \(\rho\) to the terminal object. Its \(\mathrm T_A\) pointings are classified by \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\in\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)\).

arrows.note: LoRA\(_r\hookrightarrow\) LoRA\(_{r+1}\) (the rank filtration); \(\mathrm T_A\)-pointed when \(a_0\notin\mathrm{row}\,A_0\).
DoRA with the magnitude set to the current row norms reproduces LoRA. Pointed (\(\mu_0\) = row norms of \(W_0\)); smooth wherever no row of \(W_0+sBA\) vanishes.
One stage embeds into \(K\) stages of the rebasing scheme.

LoRA\(_r\to\) PEANuT\(_{2r}\) via \(\sigma(x)-\sigma(-x)=x\), which holds for ReLU, GELU and SiLU (so the arrow is smooth for the latter two); needs \(W_0\) of full column rank (\(M^\top W_0=A\)). Pointed at \(\Theta_1=[M_0,-M_0]\), \(\Theta_2=0\).

obstructions.reason: Type I apex against Type II smooth point: the images \(\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) and \((\theta_0-P)+\mathcal M_{\le r}\) are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)).

The images agree (\(W_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\)), but \(S_1(\mathrm{LoRA})=\{XA_0\}\) has dimension \(mr\) and \(S_1(\mathrm{AdaLoRA})=\mathrm{span}\{p_iq_i^\top\}\) has dimension \(r\). LoRA is a special case of AdaLoRA only as an unpointed object.
\(d(\mathrm{LoRA}_r)=r(m+n-r)>mr=d(\text{LoRA-FA})\).

methods.check_notes: All coordinates match VIII.B (Cone r(m+n-r), T_A apex with deficit r(n-r), GL_r, GLxGL, M1, span). Arrows checked: rank filtration (T_A iff a_0 not in row A_0), DoRA with magnitude = current row norms (pointed at mu_0 = row norms of W_0), ReLoRA stage embedding, PEANuT_{2r} (M^T W_0 = A under full column rank). Obstructions to PiSSA (O3), AdaLoRA (O3, dim S_1 = r < mr) and LoRA-FA (O2) verified. Change: PEANuT arrow note: the identity sigma(x)-sigma(-x)=x also holds for GELU and SiLU (checked to 1e-15), not only ReLU.

coord_notes.kind: \(\rho_{\rm rs}(B,A)=\rho_{\rm LoRA}(\sqrt r\,B,A)\): the same object (Cor III.11(c)). The rank-stability prescription concerns how \(\alpha\) should scale with \(r\), i.e. a path through the hyperparameter torus across ranks.

methods.categorical_reading: rsLoRA is LoRA itself: the scale change is the isomorphism \(h=(\sqrt r\,B,A)\) of the slice, or equivalently a point of the hyperparameter torus (Thm III.10). Its content is a choice of trajectory \(r\mapsto(\alpha,\eta)\) across ranks, not a new object.

arrows.note: Isomorphism over \(\Theta\) (inverse \(B\mapsto B/\sqrt r\)); pointed because \(B_0=0\).

methods.check_notes: Isomorphism h(B,A) = (sqrt(r) B, A) verified: (alpha/r) sqrt(r) BA = (alpha/sqrt r) BA, pointed since B_0 = 0. All coordinates as LoRA. No changes.

coord_notes.shape: The frozen residual \(W_0-\eta B_0A_0\) moves the cone's vertex to \(W_0-P\), with \(P=\eta B_0A_0\) of rank \(r\) (the S stratum).
coord_notes.covariance: The frames come from the SVD of a sampled gradient \(G=\nabla_WL(W_0)\), so the image transforms covariantly in distribution over the data under \(O(m)\times O(n)\). Homotheties are not included: with the stable scale \(\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}/\sqrt\gamma\), \(P\propto U_{G,[r+1:2r]}V_{G,[1:r]}^\top\) does not depend on the size of \(W_0\) or \(G\), so \(W_0\mapsto cW_0\) moves the vertex to \(cW_0-P\ne c(W_0-P)\). The closest key is the spectral-frame OxO.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-GA is a Type II object: it picks the point \(P\propto U_{G,[r+1:2r]}V_{G,[1:r]}^\top\) of the stratum \(\mathcal M_r\) and moves the cone's vertex to \(\theta_0-P\), combining smoothness, gradient alignment of \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\) and a stable scale (Prop II.3). It is incomparable with zero-init LoRA.

arrows.note: Thm II.1 conversion into LoRA\(_{2r}\) on the untouched \(W_0\), pointed at the degenerate pointing \(([B_0,-B_0],[A_0;A_0])\) (product \(0\), outside the three strata).

obstructions.reason: Different points of the S stratum (gradient-SVD \(P\) against weight-SVD \(P\)) give translated cones with different vertices, hence incomparable images (Thm II.2(a),(d)).
A smooth Type II point against an apex: at equal rank the images are incomparable.

methods.check_notes: Re-derived: S stratum (Cone*, regular, GL, OxO, M1, span). Arrow into LoRA_{2r} at the (r, r, 0) pointing verified (product B_0A_0 - B_0A_0 = 0). O1 to PiSSA (different vertices) and O3 to LoRA verified. Change: covariance note refined to O(m) x O(n): the stable-scale split has a fixed magnitude, so homotheties break covariance (unlike PiSSA's CO x CO); key OxO kept.

coord_notes.kind: Same \(\rho\) as LoRA; only the rate operator \(\mathrm{diag}(\eta_AI,\lambda\eta_AI)\) changes. Under Adam (\(\varepsilon=0\), no decay, no clipping, shared schedule) and from \(B_0=0\), LoRA+ with ratio \(\lambda\) is exactly LoRA with \(\alpha\) multiplied by \(\lambda\) (Cor III.11(b)).
coord_notes.base_point: An apex in either zero-product initialisation: the paper's Init[2] (\(A=0\), \(B\) random) is the \(\mathrm T_B\) stratum, HF's default the \(\mathrm T_A\) stratum.
coord_notes.gauge: The object's gauge is \(GL_r\). Under SGD the rate ratio is the scalar gauge choice \(g=\lambda^{1/4}I\) together with an overall rate (Thm III.3).

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA+ is not a new object but a point of LoRA's hyperparameter torus: under Adam, from zero-initialised \(B\), its ratio \(\lambda\) is absorbed into \(\alpha\), so any gain must come from torus-breaking ingredients (global clipping, a shared \(\varepsilon\) or decay). Under gradient flow it moves the crossover scale \(\sigma^*\) by \(\sqrt\lambda\), and LoRA-FA is the endpoint \(\lambda\to\infty\).

arrows.note: Same object. The trajectory equivalence is the torus map \(c_B=1/\lambda\) (Adam) or \(\lambda^{-1/2}\) (SGD), which rescales \(s\); it is not an arrow.

obstructions.reason: LoRA-FA is the \(\lambda\to\infty\) endpoint of the LoRA+ dynamics, yet \(d=r(m+n-r)>mr\): the limit is dynamical, not a simulation.

methods.check_notes: Same object as LoRA (h = id), only the rate operator changes; T_A (HF) or T_B (paper Init[2]) apex; Cor III.11(b) torus reading checked. O2 obstruction to LoRA-FA (r(m+n-r) > mr) valid. No changes. Sync with the refereed paper (2026-10-03): the Cor III.11(b) equivalence is stated from B_0 = 0, the corollary's hypothesis (the paper's Init[2] starts from B != 0).

coord_notes.covariance: The frozen \(A_0\) is random, so covariance holds only in law (GL × frame).
coord_notes.rebasing: With \(A_0\) fixed it is idempotent; resampling \(A_0\) every cycle gives Flora.

methods.categorical_reading: LoRA-FA is the sub-object \(\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\hookrightarrow\mathrm{LoRA}_{(0,A_0)}\) obtained by freezing \(A\) (A2): a linear method with the same first-order image as zero-init LoRA. Its corrected gradient gives the frame-only cometric \(K(G)=\eta\,GP_V\), which depends only on \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0\) under SGD, but on \(A_0\) modulo \(B_r\) under the published AdamW.

arrows.note: Freezing \(A\) at its base value: a pointed monomorphism into LoRA pointed at \((0,A_0)\).
Isomorphism \(\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\cong\mathrm{FA}(Q)\) when \(\mathrm{row}\,A_0=\mathrm{row}\,Q\) (e.g. \(Q\) the orthonormalised \(A_0\)); for independent random frames the two agree only in law.
LoRA-FA is the first period of Flora when Flora's first projection is \(A_0\) (shared seed): one stage embeds into the rebasing scheme.

obstructions.reason: \(\mathrm{FA}(A_0)\) has image \(\{XA_0\}\) (fixed row space), MiCA's \(\mathrm{FB}(U_{\min})\) has \(\{U_{\min}Y\}\) (fixed column space); neither contains the other.

Although it starts from PiSSA's SVD, it keeps \(\theta_0\) as the residual and starts at an apex (Type I), so it is incomparable with PiSSA.

Otherwise it is a degenerate \(B_0=0\) pointing outside the three strata (Thm II.2(e)); the arrow is still pointed.

methods.categorical_reading: PiSSA is the Type II point \(P=[W_0]_r\) of the stratum \(\mathcal M_r\): the vertex moves to \(W_0-[W_0]_r\), \(\theta_0\) becomes a smooth point with full first-order reach, and the pointing is balanced at equal rates (Prop III.8). Measured from \(\theta_0\), its updates \(Y-P\) reach rank \(2r\), which is the PiSSA \(\to\) LoRA\(_{2r}\) conversion.

arrows.note: Thm II.1: PiSSA\(_r\) into LoRA\(_{2r}\) on \(W_0\) (HF's conversion), pointed at the degenerate pointing with product \(0\).

obstructions.reason: A Type II smooth point against a Type I apex at equal rank: the images are incomparable (Thm II.2(d)).
Top-\(r\) against bottom-\(r\) split: different vertices, \(W_0\) minus its top or its bottom rank-\(r\) part, so the images are incomparable.

methods.categorical_reading: OLoRA is another point of the Type II stratum, \(P=Q_rR_r\), chosen by a QR flag rather than a spectral frame. The flag privileges the first \(r\) input coordinates, so unlike PiSSA its pointing is not permutation-natural, and its charge \(\Phi_0=I/\eta_B-R_rR_r^\top/\eta_A\) is generally unbalanced.

coord_notes.shape: \(Q_T+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), started at \(B_TA_T=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q_T)\): an approximate split over a quantised residual.
coord_notes.base_point: \(\rho(q_0)=Q_T+B_TA_T\approx\theta_0\). With the default `loftq_iter=1` the defect is \(e-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\), because HF's initialiser ignores the LoRA scale \(s=\alpha/r\). It is the rank-\(r\) tail \(e-\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\) of the quantisation error only at \(s=1\), and smaller than QLoRA's defect \(e\) only for \(0<s<2\) (Prop V.2(b)).
coord_notes.covariance: The quantisation grid (blockwise NF4 scales) lives in the standard basis: Mon×Mon.
coord_notes.merge: An exact merge of the high-precision \(BA\) leaves the \(N\)-bit grid; requantising is lossy.
coord_notes.rebasing: Converges to \(\Theta\) in exact arithmetic; each merge requantises.

methods.categorical_reading: LoftQ is base change along the quantiser followed by an approximate section: it chooses \((Q,q_0)\) with \(\rho(q_0)\) close to \(\theta_0\), landing at a smooth point of the cone over \(Q_T\). With one iteration it is QLoRA's own map \(\kappa\theta_0+\mathcal M_{\le r}\), re-pointed from the apex to \(s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(\theta_0-\kappa\theta_0)=-s\,\mathrm{SVD}_r(e)\), with \(s=\alpha/r\) the LoRA scale that HF's initialiser ignores (Prop V.2(b)).

arrows.note: In the slice at the attained start \(\theta_0'=Q_T+B_TA_T\): LoftQ\(_r\) into LoRA\(_{2r}\) over \(\theta_0'\), at a degenerate pointing (as for PiSSA).

obstructions.reason: With `loftq_iter=1` both have the map \(q_N(W_0)+sBA\) and only the start differs (a rank-\(r\) point against the apex), so \(h=\mathrm{id}\) is a weak morphism, not a pointed one.
